blueprint_sources: San Francisco Mission/Potrero Hill infill — zero side setback, 3-story wood frame, underground utility service
Berkeley R-2 infill zero-lot — stacked program, no side yard, roof HVAC
SF SB9 lot split infill — 25ft wide zero-lot new construction, underground service required by DPW

petronus_classification.note: Zero-lot-line urban infill maximizes buildable footprint. No side yard means ground-level HVAC equipment is prohibited — everything goes to roof or mechanical alcoves. Underground utility service eliminates overhead drops in dense neighborhoods.

lot.note: Zero or near-zero side setbacks (0-1ft). Building footprint covers nearly the entire lot width. No ground-level side yard for equipment placement. All mechanical equipment must go to roof or be incorporated into building envelope.

structure.soft_story_note: Open ground-floor garage or large glazed opening at grade creates soft-story risk. Moment frame or structural plywood shear walls required at ground level.

floor_program.note: Compact stacked program on narrow urban lot. Vertical circulation is the spine. No side yard access forces all utility routing to front, rear, or roof.

floor_0.mep_note: Underground service enters here from street vault through exterior wall. Panel at ground floor. Stormwater management system or sump at this level. HVAC condenser NOT at grade — route to roof.

floor_1.mep_note: Kitchen wet wall rear-center. Half bath stacks below L2 bath. ERV intake/exhaust through front or rear wall — no side wall penetrations if party walls present.

floor_2.mep_note: Wet walls stack above L1. HVAC mini-split head on interior wall or ceiling cassette. Roof access hatch from this level for HVAC maintenance.

floor_3_optional.mep_note: If bath present, continue DWV stack. Mechanical penthouse or alcove here for HVAC condensers and solar inverter. Roof deck requires waterproofing over structural deck.

wet_wall.stormwater_note: Zero lot coverage means no natural drainage. Rainwater catchment, permeable paver drainage zones, or sump/retention system required. Coordinate stormwater outfall with wet wall and building drain location.
wet_wall.note: Stack runs vertically through rear-center partition. Kitchen L1 and all baths align to this stack. DWV exits slab at rear toward street via sewer lateral.

staircase.mep_note: Stair along center spine. Wet wall on opposite side (rear). Vertical MEP chases in stair wall cavity. No side access means front and rear exterior walls are the only options for equipment penetrations.

mep_chase.note: Zero side setback: no equipment on ground at sides. All vertical MEP in interior walls. Underground service enters from front or rear — plan conduit route from street vault through exterior wall to panel location before finalizing floor layout.

hvac.ground_mount_prohibition: CRITICAL: No side yard space exists for ground-mounted condensers. Do not place any HVAC outdoor equipment at grade. Default to roof-mounted units, slim-line side-discharge heat pumps in mechanical alcoves, or rooftop mini-split condensers.

stormwater.note: Impervious footprint covers entire lot — no natural infiltration. SF and Oakland require on-site stormwater retention or slow-release. Design sump or cistern at or below slab level. Route roof leaders to cistern or perforated trench drain at rear.

panel.underground_service_note: New construction in SF, Berkeley, Oakland typically requires undergrounding of utility service. Route service conductors in conduit from street vault, up through exterior foundation wall, to interior panel location. Coordinate with PG&E or local utility for vault location.

solar.note: Flat or low-slope roof in urban infill. Coordinate solar array footprint with rooftop HVAC equipment.

fire_sprinklers.applicable_rule: SF requires sprinklers for new construction >2 stories. Oakland requires per local amendment.

massing_hints.note: Slim vertical urban form. Footprint fills lot width completely. Facade is a single front plane with punched openings or large glazing. Rear facade opens to small rear yard or garden. Rooftop penthouse volume houses HVAC and solar.

known_constraints_summary: GROUND CONDENSER PROHIBITED: Zero side setback means no space for outdoor AC/heat pump units at grade. All condensers must go to roof. Design roof mechanical alcove before finalizing floor plan.
Underground utility service required: new builds cannot use overhead drop — plan conduit route from street vault through exterior wall to panel location.
Stormwater management required: zero permeable ground surface means on-site cistern, sump, or slow-release retention system is needed.
No side wall penetrations if party walls present — ERV/HRV, HVAC, and utility penetrations go front or rear only.
Fire sprinklers required for new construction >2 stories in SF and Oakland (local amendment).
Soft story risk at open ground-floor garage — structural moment frame or shear walls required.
Seismic design category D — full shear wall design despite narrow lot width.
Roof real estate must serve: solar PV + HVAC condensers + ERV terminations + possible roof deck — generate roof plan early.
DWV stack at rear-center interior wall — gravity path must clear stormwater system in slab.
Underground service conduit adds cost and space at ground floor — factor into entry and utility room layout.
